title: OpenAI Disbands Robotics Team as General-Purpose Models Take Over
summary: OpenAI disbanded its standalone robotics team, folding researchers into core divisions as general-purpose models outperform specialized robot AI. Here's what it signals about AI strategy, the benchmark data, and the 2027 humanoid robot timeline.

# OpenAI Disbands Robotics Team as General-Purpose Models Take Over


By OpenTools Team


·


November 15, 2026


OpenAI dissolved its standalone robotics research team on November 13, folding staff into its core research and applied divisions. The reason: GPT‑6 Astra already outperforms specialized robot models on manipulation benchmarks, and the company is betting that embodied AI is just another application of general intelligence — not a separate discipline.


## What Happened: The Team Dissolved, the Hardware Ambition Stays


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) confirmed to[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/) on November 13, 2026 that it dissolved its standalone robotics team and reassigned all staff across the company. The split goes two ways: robotics *research* staff now report to Chief Research Officer Mark Chen inside the main research organization, while applied robotics and *hardware* teams moved to the Applied organization under President Greg Brockman.


No layoffs were reported. Headcount of the affected team remains undisclosed. The company had already booked a booth at the CoRL robotics conference in Austin — **booth #208 sat empty** . A spokesperson told Fortune that robotics "remains a core part of OpenAI's long-term vision," while the company described the reorganization as an acceleration, not a retreat.


This is OpenAI's **second** robotics team shutdown. The first was in 2020, when cofounder Wojciech Zaremba cited limited robot data. The team was rebuilt as a standalone unit in 2024. This time, the reason is the opposite: general models got good enough,[MLQ.ai](https://mlq.ai/news/openai-disbands-its-standalone-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots-fortune-reports/) reported.


## The Benchmark That Changed the Calculus


The decision was driven by a specific benchmark result. In a study run by[Nvidia](https://opentools.ai/organizations/nvidia) , researchers gave **[GPT-6 Astra](https://opentools.ai/llms/gpt-6-astra)** camera images, robot state information, and a control interface for commanding a simulated robot's actions. Astra scored a **74.8% success rate** on a simulated manipulation task. The best specialized robotics models on the same leaderboard scored **51.0%** — a 23.8 percentage-point gap, per[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/) .


If a general-purpose model that also does code generation, legal analysis, and financial modeling can outperform purpose-built robot AI by nearly 24 points, the argument for maintaining a separate robotics AI team collapses.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's thesis: robotics is becoming a downstream application of general intelligence — like coding or document analysis — rather than its own discipline requiring specialized models.


## The Competitive Split: General-Purpose vs. Specialized


The field is splitting along a clear fault line.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) is betting on **general-purpose models applied to robotics.[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) DeepMind is taking the **specialized approach** with purpose-built robot models,[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/) notes.**


**Figure AI made the earliest and most dramatic bet against platform dependence. Figure ended its partnership with OpenAI in February 2025, with founder Brett Adcock citing a "major breakthrough on fully end-to-end robot AI" developed in-house, as[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/02/04/figure-drops-openai-in-favor-of-in-house-models/) reported at the time. That decision looks prescient now that OpenAI folded its own robotics AI team.**


**Academic researchers are split too. CMU's Guanya Shi told Fortune that robotics is "no longer a special problem" but a downstream application of general intelligence — though he warns cloud-hosted models are too slow for physical control, requiring small onboard models. MIT's Russ Tedrake, cofounder of Walden Robotics, argues robot makers keep an edge from real-world deployment data that general models can't access. Pete Florence of Generalist says it's "unclear that any existing model would be the one that dominates robotics in the long-run,"[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/) reported.**


## **The Financial Context: A $10.9B Loss and an IPO Looming**


**The reorganization has a financial dimension that[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) isn't emphasizing publicly. The company reported **$10.9 billion in operating losses** last quarter, and a 2027 IPO is widely expected, according to[The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/openai-robotics-spinout-ipo-2026) (May 4, 2026).**


**Dissolving a standalone team — even without layoffs — consolidates headcount under existing leadership, removes a separate cost center line, and strengthens the "we're a general intelligence company" narrative for public markets. In May 2026,[The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/openai-robotics-spinout-ipo-2026) reported that OpenAI had shelved plans to spin out its robotics and consumer hardware units, because the businesses would still have to be consolidated on its financial statements.**


**Investors are scrutinizing every cost center at the major AI labs. A standalone robotics team that can be absorbed into existing org structures while maintaining the same hardware ambitions is an easy efficiency win on paper — especially when the technical argument (general models already outperform specialized ones) supports it.**


## **What Comes Next: The 2027 Humanoid Robot Target**


**[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) is not walking away from hardware. Sam Altman is targeting a **first public demonstration of OpenAI's own humanoid robot in 2027** ,[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/13/openai-disbands-robotics-team-as-its-general-models-start-running-robots/) reported. The bet is that rather than building specialized robot AI models, the company feeds camera images, robot state, and control interfaces directly into its general frontier models.**


**The research team under Mark Chen is expected to improve the general model's embodied reasoning capability, while the Applied team under Greg Brockman handles the hardware build. This mirrors OpenAI's approach to code generation: no separate "coding model," just the general model applied to code.**


**The open question is latency. Astra's 74.8% benchmark was in simulation. Real-time physical control requires sub-100ms response times, and cloud-hosted models currently operate in the 500ms–2s range. CMU's Shi flagged this explicitly: cloud inference latency is a real barrier to physical deployment regardless of benchmark scores. Until OpenAI closes that gap — likely with onboard compute rather than cloud — the humanoid robot remains a demonstration target rather than a shipping product.**


## **What It Means for Builders**


**The signal for developers is clear: the AI stack is collapsing.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's bet is that the same API you use for code generation, document analysis, and chat will eventually control robot arms — and that specialized robot AI middleware becomes unnecessary.**


**For builders working at the intersection of AI and physical automation, this has two implications. First, you may not need a separate robotics stack — the general model API may suffice for high-leel reasoning about physical tasks. Second, latency remains the unsolved problem, which means **small onboard models and edge inference** are where the real engineering work lives for the foreseeable future.**


**The most important signal is organizational, not technical: when OpenAI dissolves a team twice, it's saying that team's structure was the bottleneck, not its mission. The hardware ambition survived both shutdowns. The dedicated org structure didn't. Builders should read this as: embodied AI is real and coming, but it won't require a separate toolchain.**
